classification.difficultyReason: Combine vertex form, exact surd intercepts and concavity to construct labelled sketches.

content.prompt: Sketch the graph of each quadratic, clearly labelling the $x$- and $y$-intercepts, the axis of symmetry and the vertex.

answer.worked:
The vertex is $(3,4)$ and the axis of symmetry is $x=3$.

At $x=0$:
$$\begin{align*}y&=(0-3)^2+4\\y&=13\end{align*}$$
Thus the $y$-intercept is $(0,13)$. Since $(x-3)^2\geq0$, $y\geq4$, so there are no $x$-intercepts. Sketch an upward-opening parabola through the labelled features.

spec.description: Complete upward-opening solution graph with vertex, y-intercept and dashed axis of symmetry; no x-intercepts.

answer.worked:
The vertex is $(-1,-6)$ and the axis of symmetry is $x=-1$.

At $x=0$:
$$\begin{align*}y&=3(0+1)^2-6\\y&=-3\end{align*}$$
For the $x$-intercepts, set $y=0$:
$$\begin{align*}3(x+1)^2-6&=0\\3(x+1)^2&=6\\(x+1)^2&=2\\x+1&=\pm\sqrt2\\x&=-1\pm\sqrt2\end{align*}$$
Sketch an upward-opening parabola through $(-1-\sqrt2,0)$, $(-1+\sqrt2,0)$ and $(0,-3)$, with vertex $(-1,-6)$.

answer.worked:
The vertex is $(-3,5)$ and the axis of symmetry is $x=-3$.

At $x=0$:
$$\begin{align*}y&=5-(0+3)^2\\y&=-4\end{align*}$$
For the $x$-intercepts:
$$\begin{align*}5-(x+3)^2&=0\\(x+3)^2&=5\\x+3&=\pm\sqrt5\\x&=-3\pm\sqrt5\end{align*}$$
Sketch a downward-opening parabola through $(-3-\sqrt5,0)$, $(-3+\sqrt5,0)$ and $(0,-4)$, with vertex $(-3,5)$.

spec.description: Complete downward-opening graph with exact root labels, y-intercept, vertex and dashed axis of symmetry.

answer.worked:
The vertex is $(5,6)$ and the axis of symmetry is $x=5$.

At $x=0$:
$$\begin{align*}y&=6-3(0-5)^2\\y&=6-75\\y&=-69\end{align*}$$
For the $x$-intercepts:
$$\begin{align*}6-3(x-5)^2&=0\\3(x-5)^2&=6\\(x-5)^2&=2\\x-5&=\pm\sqrt2\\x&=5\pm\sqrt2\end{align*}$$
Sketch a downward-opening parabola through $(5-\sqrt2,0)$, $(5+\sqrt2,0)$ and $(0,-69)$, with vertex $(5,6)$.
